# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👌 👍 👌 👍 👍 👍]

I can see the bomb’s external information but cannot operate it. The display reads 0, the light is blue, and the embossed warning says “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” There are three wires in order: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I am sending these facts to the Mute and Blind so the manual and physical controls can be matched safely. The gestures from the Mute do not alter any bomb information I can see.

```text
speak(text="The display reads 0. The light is blue. The bomb is embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, and wire 3 is blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, blue light, embossed “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” and wires red, green, blue in positions 1–3. I cannot interpret the Mute’s two 👍 gestures as a manual instruction, so I will not infer an action from them. I’m repeating the visible state to the Blind, who can operate the bomb if the manual identifies a safe non-wire control.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="State unchanged: display 0, light blue, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Do not cut any wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

The visible state is still unchanged, and the warning rules out all wire-cutting actions. The two repeated 👍 gestures may be acknowledgements, but they do not identify a safe control. I will establish a clear yes/no protocol with the Mute: 👍 means yes and 👎 means no, asking whether the manual calls for pressing a control rather than cutting a wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb is unchanged: display 0, blue light, warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red green blue. Use one gesture for each answer: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no. Does the manual instruct Blind to press a button or switch?")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb is unchanged: display 0, blue light, warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red green blue. Do not cut any wire. Please wait for the Mute's manual-based instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute’s 👎 answers “no” to my question about pressing a button or switch. The warning still forbids cutting wires, so I will narrow down the permitted physical action using the established yes/no gesture protocol. I’ll ask whether the manual calls for turning a knob or dial.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I read your 👎 as no: do not press a button or switch. New yes/no question: does the manual instruct Blind to turn a knob or dial? Reply 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual does not call for pressing a button or switch. Do not cut wires. Wait while I identify the permitted control.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute’s latest 👎 means the manual does not call for turning a knob or dial. The only established constraints are that no wire may be cut and neither pressing a button/switch nor turning a knob/dial is correct. I’ll test another distinct control type without asking Blind to act prematurely.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I read your 👎 as no: do not turn a knob or dial. New yes/no question: does the manual instruct Blind to pull a lever or handle? Reply 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual rules out cutting wires, pressing a button or switch, and turning a knob or dial. Do not act yet; we are identifying the correct control.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute’s 👎 rules out pulling a lever or handle as well. No permitted action has yet been identified, and the embossed warning still prohibits cutting any wire. I will ask whether the manual requires holding a control, while telling the Blind not to manipulate anything until the instruction is confirmed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I read your 👎 as no: do not pull a lever or handle. New yes/no question: does the manual instruct Blind to hold or keep holding a control? Reply 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual has ruled out cutting wires, pressing a button or switch, turning a knob or dial, and pulling a lever or handle. Do not manipulate the bomb until the correct action is confirmed.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute’s 👎 means the manual does not instruct Blind to hold a control. The bomb still gives no indication that any previously tested action is safe. I’ll check the opposite kind of sustained action—releasing a control—without asking Blind to touch anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I read your 👎 as no: do not hold a control. New yes/no question: does the manual instruct Blind to release or let go of a control? Reply 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual has not identified a safe action. Do not manipulate the bomb yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute’s 👎 rules out releasing or letting go of a control. Every proposed physical operation so far has been rejected, while the bomb remains unchanged and wire cutting is explicitly forbidden. The safest remaining possibility is that the manual requires no manipulation—waiting for a condition or sequence—so I will ask that directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I read your 👎 as no: do not release or let go of a control. Does the manual instruct Blind to take no action and wait? Reply 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="All proposed physical operations have been ruled out, and no wire may be cut. Do not manipulate the bomb. I am checking whether the manual says to take no action and wait.")
wait()
```
